top_signals.title: Gold Slumps as Hormuz Impasse Keeps Rate-Hike Bets Elevated
top_signals.summary: Gold slumped as an impasse over the Strait of Hormuz kept energy costs elevated and maintained pressure on the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates further to combat sticky inflation.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Inflation expectations impacting rate path, bonds and global risk assets.

top_signals.title: North Korea’s Irregular Warfare After Ukraine
top_signals.summary:
Pyongyang has a long history of conducting irregular warfare and asymmetric operations: Look no further than the 1968 Blue House raid or the 1996 submarine incursion as the most pressing examples. More often than not, North Korea failed to achieve the intended objectives of its missions and lost its commandos. Despite failures, the regime pressed on, and now, over thirty years after the sub incursion, it has the combat experience of its special operations forces in Kursk to leverage. top_signals.title: Vietnam Jewelry Giant PNJ Forecasts Loss After Diamond Scandal
top_signals.summary: Phu Nhuan Jewelry JSC, Vietnam’s largest listed jewelry retailer, plans to slash its 2026 revenue target and forecasts a 6.27 trillion dong ($241 million) loss as it sets aside a huge provision for customer buybacks following a diamond-smuggling scandal.

top_signals.title: President von der Leyen announces €710 million to support displaced people in Africa and global crisis relief
top_signals.summary: European Commission Press release New York, 26 Sep 2026 As the 81st UN General Assembly High Level Week draws to a close in New York, President of the European Commission Ursula von der Leyen announced almost €710 million in EU support to displaced people and communities in Sub-Saharan Africa, as well as emergency assistance to people affected by crises worldwide. The announcement was made as part of international advocacy organisation Global Citizen's campaign.
